about: The game's terms, one rendering per language (the first is the one to use; any listed is accepted by the check). checks/i18n.mjs requires a term's rendering in a translation wherever the English message uses one of its forms, for terms with check true; a key in except is let off. zh-TW is Taiwan usage, translated directly, never converted from zh-Hans. Notes say why a rendering was picked; change one only with a DECISIONS.md line, then sweep the translations that use it.
keep: $ and the money figures' k, M and B
line symbols and line, station and city names the player or the data gave
km, m, mi, ft, mph, km/h

terms.meaning: A journey people want to make between two places, by any means: what demand counts. Never the player's service.
terms.notes: Kept apart from ride/rider (乗車, 乘客), as Anita keeps trips and rides apart. ja counts with 回 (1日12,400回), zh with 人次. zh-TW: 出行 reads as a mainland word in Taiwan; 旅次 is Taiwan's own transport word (通勤旅次, 旅次需求).

terms.meaning: A person riding the player's lines; only for what happens on the player's system.
terms.notes: ja 利用者 where it means people using a station rather than people on a train.

terms.meaning: One journey on the player's lines, as a count.
terms.notes: Also a verb (to ride). Counts read naturally as 人次 (zh) and 乗車 or 人 (ja); zh-TW 運量 is the usual word for a line's ridership.

terms.meaning: People getting on trains at a station, a count per day.
terms.notes: ja 乗車人員 is the railways' own word in station statistics; 乗車人数 is plainer.

terms.meaning: How many trips people want to make, between which places, and how many would take the player's trains.
A service the player runs: trains, buses or boats on a fixed list of stops.
terms.notes: Not the drawn track (線路 in ja is track, not line). 線 alone after a name (山手線, 1号线). ja 航路 for a ferry line only.

terms.meaning: A place on the track where trains stop, with one platform or more.
The part of a station beside the track where riders get on and off.
terms.notes: zh-TW 月台, not the mainland 站台.

terms.meaning: A station a line calls at (noun).
terms.notes: Also the verb (trains stop, stop running), so not checked.

terms.meaning: The rails the player draws and builds, blueprint or constructed.
terms.notes: Single, double and quadruple track as railways say them (単線 / 单线 / 單線, 複線 / 双线 / 雙軌, 複々線 / 四线 / 四線); zh-TW 單軌 is a monorail, never single track.

terms.meaning: Track and stations drawn but not yet constructed or paid for; free to change.
terms.notes: As planned lines are called (計画線, 规划线路). 蓝图 avoided: in other games it means a copy-and-paste template.

terms.meaning: Turn a blueprint into real track, paying for it at once; once constructed, removing it refunds nothing.
terms.notes: The Construct button is 着工 / 开工 / 動工: the moment money is committed, kept apart from Build (the tab and tools, which also draw blueprints: 建設 / 建造 / 建造). Constructed is 建設済み / 已建成 / 已完工; construction cost 建設費 / 建造费用 / 興建費用.

terms.meaning: Constructed: real track or a real station, as against blueprint.
terms.notes: Build (the tab, the tools) is the general word and covers blueprint too: 建設, 建造, 建造.

terms.meaning: What a rider pays for a trip on the player's lines; set by the player per km.
terms.notes: Fare income 運賃収入 / 票款收入 / 票箱收入.

terms.meaning: The daily cost of keeping track and stations, whether trains run or not.
The cost of running trains, per train-km and per car-km.
terms.notes: zh-TW 營運費用 avoided: 營運 reads as all operating costs, upkeep included, and profit is fares minus both.

terms.meaning: Fares in minus running costs and upkeep, over a day.
terms.notes: A loss is 赤字 / 亏损 / 虧損.

terms.meaning: The money the player has to spend.
terms.notes: As rail building games name it (A列車で行こう's 資金).

terms.meaning: Money borrowed, paid back from the cash.
terms.notes: ja 借入金 for the amount owed.

terms.meaning: Minutes between trains on a line.
terms.notes: zh-TW 班距 is what Taipei Metro posts.

terms.meaning: How many trains a line runs each way in an hour.
terms.notes: 毎時12本, 每小时12班, 每小時12班.

terms.meaning: One car of a train; trains are 1 to 16 cars long.
terms.notes: English car also means an automobile (the next term); read the context. 8両編成, 8节车厢, 8節車廂.

terms.meaning: People driving instead of taking a train; demand's other mode.
terms.notes: By car 車で / 开车 / 開車; a mode share 自動車分担率 / 汽车分担率 / 汽車分擔率.

terms.meaning: More riders on a train than its rated load.
Riders on a train as a share of its rated capacity (Average load).
terms.notes: ja 乗車率 as Japanese railways publish it (乗車率150%). zh-TW 承載率 as Taiwan's metros say. Also loading data (読み込み / 加载 / 載入).

terms.meaning: How many riders or trains something can take: a train's rated load, a track's trains an hour.
terms.notes: A train's rated load is 定員 / 载客量 / 載客量. zh-TW never 運量, which in Taiwan is ridership, the opposite figure.

terms.meaning: Changing from one line to another on a trip.
terms.notes: zh-TW 轉乘, not the mainland 换乘/換乘. ja 乗継 for a transfer fare (乗継運賃).

terms.meaning: A walkway the player builds joining two stations, so riders change between them.
Stations joined by passages or a building, treated as one place to change lines.
terms.notes: What riders call a place to change lines (乗換駅, 换乘站, 轉乘站); 駅群 / 车站群 where the stations as a group are meant. Not 站群, a word for SEO site networks.

terms.meaning: An outline the player draws that joins the stations inside it into one complex.
terms.notes: 站房 is Chinese railways' word for a station building; Taiwan says 站體.

terms.meaning: A place with its own demand: a zone, shown as a city or a stretch of countryside.
Demand's unit of area; the player mostly sees zones as cities.
terms.notes: ja keeps the katakana as a game unit; 地域 would read as any region.

terms.meaning: Trips between cities, as against trips within one.
Trips between home and work or school.
terms.notes: ja 通勤・通学 where school is meant too; zh 通勤 covers both loosely.

terms.meaning: Why a trip is made: work, school, errands, visits and the rest.
terms.notes: Trip purpose 移動目的 / 出行目的 / 旅次目的.

terms.meaning: The share of trips that go by the player's trains rather than by car.
terms.notes: The planners' modal split word, short enough for a label; 分担率 alone once the train is clear from the panel.

terms.meaning: Urban rail, mostly underground.
terms.notes: metro area means a city region (都市圏, 都市圈, 都會區).

terms.meaning: Bus lines the player runs on roads.
terms.notes: zh-Hans 公交 (公交线路, 公交车); zh-TW 公車, not 巴士 (Hong Kong).

terms.meaning: Boat lines the player runs between ports.
terms.notes: ja 船 or 航路 where a small passenger boat is meant; フェリー suggests a car ferry.

terms.meaning: A ferry line's stop on the shore.
terms.notes: A ferry stop is a pier (码头), not a seaport (港口).

terms.meaning: Track and trains built for high speeds, costing more.
terms.notes: Not 新幹線, a brand.

terms.meaning: Track raised on columns above the ground.
Track under the ground, bored deep or cut and cover.
Shallow tunnel built by digging down from the street.
terms.notes: The engineers' words (開削工法, 明挖法).

terms.meaning: A junction where one track crosses another at a different level.
terms.notes: A flat junction is 平面交差 / 平交 / 平交.

terms.meaning: A pair of switches letting trains move between two side-by-side tracks.
A junction where tracks cross or branch at the same level, so trains take turns.
terms.notes: Railway usage; not checked, so a message can say it the way the panel reads best.

terms.meaning: Where track branches or tracks meet.
terms.notes: The place, not the switch itself (分岐器 / 道岔).

terms.meaning: A station upgrade: sidings past the platforms where trains turn back.
terms.notes: The upgrade is the turnback track, not a terminus station (終着駅).

terms.meaning: A train's run out to the far end of its line and back, as a time.
terms.notes: Never the trip term (移動 / 出行 / 旅次): a round trip is the train's, not people's.

terms.meaning: A station upgrade: extra track where a train can wait while another passes.
terms.notes: Mainland metros say 越行线 (越行站); Taiwan's railways say 待避, as Japan does.

terms.meaning: Something bought for a station that raises its capacity or makes it nicer to use.
terms.notes: ja 改良 (駅改良) over the katakana アップグレード.

terms.meaning: A line's trains and headways through each period of the day.
One of the five parts of the day schedules and demand are set by.
The score lines earn each hour.
terms.notes: Also the points a track or bus route is drawn through (点).

terms.meaning: A goal met, with a medal.
terms.notes: Steam's words in each language.

terms.meaning: A game mode with no money limits and no leaderboard.
A stored game, in the browser or as a file; also the verb.
terms.notes: The noun is セーブデータ / 存档 / 存檔, the verb 保存 / 保存 / 儲存.

terms.meaning: Walking to and from stations, part of a trip.
